source: Curated from agent-research literature (Voyager, Reflexion, GITM, JARVIS-1, DEPS, MemGPT, ReAct, Generative Agents, CRITIC) and Anthropic's effective-agents writeups, re-mapped to the Mindcraft codebase as of 2026-05-04. Note: a SessionMemory layer (src/agent/session_memory.js) now sits between History.memory and the prompt and surfaces objective summary, last failure code, recovery hint, current resource target, and pending tasks into $MEMORY — so several earlier 'add a placeholder' quick wins are partially shipped.

quick_wins.title: Surface a rolling window of recent failures, not just the last one
quick_wins.summary: session_memory already exposes lastCommandResultCode + lastFailureReason + nextRecommendedRecoveryCommand into $MEMORY. The remaining gap is a SHORT history of the last 2-3 failures (code + summary) so the model sees patterns like 'three ERR_NO_PATH in a row' rather than only the most recent. Add session_memory.recentFailures (capped at 3) populated in noteCommandResult and rendered inside formatSessionMemory.

quick_wins.title: Replace the 500-char History.memory truncation with labeled buckets
quick_wins.summary: history.js still hard-truncates this.memory to 500 chars mid-sentence (history.js:67-70). Now that session_memory carries the operationally hot state, History.memory should hold longer-lived facts — split it into FACTS / OPEN_GOALS / MISTAKES_TO_AVOID buckets each capped independently, rendered into $TEXT_MEMORY. Update the saving_memory profile prompt to emit those sections.

quick_wins.title: Resolve the one-command policy mismatch
quick_wins.summary: Agent.handleMessage now extracts and executes every command in one model response (agent.js:506-577), but the default prompt and command docs still say 'Use at most one command in each response.' Decide whether serial multi-command execution is supported behavior or only a defensive fallback, then align tests, prompts, and UI docs so the model is not trained against the runtime.

quick_wins.title: Render the full ObjectiveStack into the prompt, not just the top frame
quick_wins.summary: session_memory.activeObjectiveSummary already injects the TOP objective into $MEMORY (and resolveMaxResponses uses it for the cap policy), but ObjectiveStack.getSummary() produces a multi-frame view that is still only visible via !objectives. Add an $OBJECTIVE_STACK placeholder in replaceStrings that emits getSummary(), or extend formatSessionMemory to render up to 3 frames.

quick_wins.title: Detect repeated failing commands and inject a sharp interrupt
quick_wins.summary: session_memory now stores lastCommandResultCode, but consecutive identical failures still re-enter the loop with no extra signal. Hash the last N (commandName, code) pairs in handleMessage. If the same pair repeats, append a system turn 'You just tried X and it failed with ERR_Y. Try a different approach or ask for help.' before the next promptConvo call.

quick_wins.title: Lock down session_memory rendering in unit tests
quick_wins.summary: test/situational_memory.test.js exists but the session_memory surface has grown (pendingTasks, recordMiningCompletion writes to memory_bank). Add deterministic tests asserting that (a) noteUserIntent populates pendingTasks for ore phrases, (b) noteCommandResult flips pending status to active/done/pending across success/fail, (c) formatSessionMemory emits the expected order. This is the cheapest way to keep $MEMORY shape stable while the system grows.

themes.title: Reasoning Loop & Control Flow
themes.summary: The current loop now supports serial command extraction, goal-aware response caps, and a session_memory layer that carries last failure / recovery hint into the next prompt. Still no explicit reflect/replan step. Voyager, Reflexion, and DEPS all show that adding a structured observe -> reflect -> act beat dramatically improves long-horizon success in Minecraft.

recommendations.title: Insert a Reflexion turn after K consecutive non-progress steps
recommendations.detail: Track 'progress' as inventory delta + objective-state changes between handleMessage iterations. After 3 iterations with no progress (or 3 consecutive ERR_* in session_memory), run a dedicated promptReflection() call (separate from promptConvo) whose output is prepended to history as a system note. Reflexion shows even a single verbal self-critique buffer materially improves trial-2 performance with no weight updates. session_memory.recentFailures (see qw-recent-failures-window) is the natural trigger signal.

recommendations.title: Harden DEPS planning for !newAction with JSON validation
recommendations.detail: A DEPS-style promptNewActionPlan now runs before promptCoding and its raw output is injected into Coder via _formatNewActionPlanForCoding (coder.js:31-160). The next gap is validating that the planner returns parseable JSON with goal, sub_goals, selected_sub_goal, and selection_reason, then falling back or re-prompting when it does not. Without validation, bad planner text becomes binding context for code generation.

recommendations.title: Make replanning a first-class trigger, not an implicit retry
recommendations.detail: Add explicit triggers: action timeout (already in ActionManager._startTimeout at action_manager.js:203-214), 3+ failed commands in a row (now trivially derivable from session_memory), death event, inventory shrinkage during a gather objective. Each should call objectives.updateTop({state: 'REPLAN'}) and emit a system message that explains WHY — otherwise the model has to infer from raw output why the loop broke.

recommendations.title: Separate 'thought' from 'action' parsing (ReAct-style)
recommendations.detail: Right now any non-command text in a model reply is treated as chat (or as a pre-message before the command, depending on settings.show_command_syntax — agent.js:541-559). Adopt a 'Thought: … Action: !cmd(…)' format and either hide or chat the Thought. Gives the model explicit room to reason without leaking it into in-game chat, and lets you log the reasoning trace separately in TranscriptLogger for replay/eval.

recommendations.title: Track explicit progress signal in session_memory and gate the cap on it
recommendations.detail: resolveMaxResponses already uses ObjectiveStack status. The natural next move is a session_memory.progressSinceLastTurn flag derived from inventory delta + objective state change, used to (a) lower the response cap when no progress is made, and (b) trigger reflection (see rl-reflexion). Today the cap policy and the reasoning context can drift from each other when the objective is 'pending' but the bot is actually stuck.

themes.title: Tool / Command Output Design
themes.summary: Mindcraft now has a normalization/rendering layer for command results (normalizeCommandResult / renderCommandResult), stable OK/ERR_* prefixes, and next_hints flowing into session_memory.nextRecommendedRecoveryCommand. The next leverage is making outputs compact, structured, and consistently recoverable across all command implementations.

recommendations.title: Finish migrating commands to structured results before rendering
recommendations.detail: commands/index.js now normalizes any return into {ok, code, summary, data, next_hints, raw} (commands/index.js:270-323), and several objective/route/storage paths emit structured-looking results. Finish the migration so every command returns the object shape first, with renderCommandResult as the only prompt-facing text renderer. This gives evals machine-readable result data and gives the model consistent recovery hints via next_hints.

recommendations.title: Move action-output truncation into the shared result renderer
recommendations.detail: ActionManager.getBotOutputSummary now keeps both the first and final ~250 chars (action_manager.js:187-201), which fixes the old middle-loss problem. The remaining issue is that truncation happens before command normalization and is capped at 500 chars with no structured error fields. Move this into the command-result renderer so failures preserve code, summary, tail, and next_hints predictably.

recommendations.title: Document recovery semantics for ERR_* codes in $COMMAND_DOCS
recommendations.detail: Stable codes now exist in normalizeCommandResult (commands/index.js:33-41 plus dynamic ERR_* from _codeFromReason). next_hints are surfaced into session_memory. The next step is a small recovery table in $COMMAND_DOCS so the model also sees the semantics directly: ERR_NO_PATH -> try nearer waypoint or ask; ERR_BAD_ARGS -> inspect docs; ERR_PARTIAL -> continue from reported state. Codes are most useful when paired with explicit next moves.

recommendations.title: Make $STATS and $INVENTORY diff-style after the first call
recommendations.detail: Prompter.replaceStrings rebuilds full $STATS/$INVENTORY every prompt; in self-prompt loops these are 90% identical between turns. Cache the previous render and emit only the delta for steps 2..N of one handleMessage, with a periodic full snapshot every 5 turns. Saves serious tokens on long autonomous runs. Note: stableReplacements already caches inside one promptConvo retry burst — extend the cache scope to the whole reasoning loop instead of one retry.

recommendations.title: Add !abortObjective(reason), distinct from !stop and !clearObjectives
recommendations.detail: The repo has !clearObjectives for cancelling the stack, but the model still lacks a way to mark the top objective as failed with a reason. Add !abortObjective('reason') that pops or updates the top frame with status failed and records the reason to transcript/memory and to session_memory.lastFailureReason. That preserves learning signal instead of simply clearing state.

themes.title: Memory Architectures
themes.summary: Mindcraft now has THREE memory layers: a 500-char History.memory (semantic running summary), typed MemoryBank namespaces (places / journeymap / routes / storage / observations / pending — now also written by mining_objective.recordMiningCompletion), and per-session SessionMemory (objective, last command, pending tasks, last failure, recovery hint). It still has no semantic retrieval and no durable episodic store separate from the chat archive.

recommendations.title: Add a durable episodic store; keep History.memory for semantic facts
recommendations.detail: session_memory already covers 'working memory' (current objective + active task state). Add an episodic store: timestamped {event, outcome, code, frame_id} entries written from ObjectiveStack.pop and noteCommandResult on terminal transitions (success/failure). Persist to bots/{name}/episodic.jsonl. Render the most recent K entries into a new $EPISODIC placeholder, distinct from $TEXT_MEMORY. JARVIS-1 shows this split is what enables life-long task transfer.

recommendations.title: Retrieve episodic memories by similarity to the current goal
recommendations.detail: Reuse the Examples.embed pipeline: embed every episodic entry on write, and at prompt-build time embed the active objective + last user message and pull top-k episodes into $EPISODIC. Essentially MemGPT's recall memory pattern; replaces the current 'shove the running summary in every prompt' approach.

recommendations.title: Add a reflection step that promotes episodic facts to semantic ones
recommendations.detail: After every Nth completed objective, run a promptReflect over recent episodic entries and extract durable facts (e.g. 'creepers blow up villager workstations' → semantic, written into History.memory FACTS bucket from qw-structured-memory-buckets). This is the Generative Agents reflection loop — what stops agents from re-learning the same lesson every play session.

recommendations.title: Garbage-collect MemoryBank by recency + utility, per namespace
recommendations.detail: MemoryBank stores typed namespaces, not just places, and is now written by objective code (mining_objective.recordMiningCompletion appends one observations entry per successful mine — these grow without bound). Add usage timestamps and namespace-specific pruning rules while always preserving last_death_position, home_chest, active routes, and recent pending issues. observations is the most urgent namespace to bound.

recommendations.title: Persist a 'lessons learned' file across bot processes
recommendations.detail: Create bots/{name}/lessons.jsonl appended whenever a reflection extracts a semantic fact, and load it into a $LESSONS placeholder at prompt-build time. The Voyager skill-library idea applied to negative knowledge — what NOT to do, in addition to what to do. Pairs naturally with session_memory.recentFailures: a recurring failure pattern is the trigger to write a lesson.

themes.title: Example Retrieval & Prompt Steering
themes.summary: examples.js does embedding-based retrieval with a word-overlap fallback, normalizeIntentText preprocessing, assistant-output overlap, and a small user-intent role boost. Biggest gaps are hybrid scoring tuning, negative examples, and intent classification before retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add hybrid BM25 + embedding scoring with a learned weight
recommendations.detail: embeddingScore mixes cosine similarity with assistant-output word overlap and a small role boost; fallbackScore uses intent/output word overlap. Replace the word-overlap component with proper BM25 over the example corpus and store the blend weight in profile so you can sweep it. Hybrid retrieval consistently beats pure dense on small heterogeneous corpora — exactly Mindcraft's regime.

recommendations.title: Classify intent before retrieving examples
recommendations.detail: normalizeIntentText strips noise but still sends raw text to embed(). Add a tiny pre-classifier (LLM or rules) that tags the latest user message as one of {social, build, gather, navigate, combat, query, debug} and pull k examples from each bucket weighted by predicted distribution. Avoids 'help me kill this zombie' pulling a mining example just because both mention iron. session_memory.pendingTasks already encodes 'gather' intent for ore commands — extend that signal to other categories.

recommendations.title: Add negative / anti-examples to the conversing prompt
recommendations.detail: Currently $EXAMPLES are all 'do this'. Add a separate $ANTI_EXAMPLES section showing 2 prior failed trajectories (pulled from the lessons store / episodic store) with annotations like 'Wrong because the bot didn't check inventory first'. CRITIC and Anthropic's tool-design guidance both note a few well-labeled negatives outperform many positives on tool-call accuracy.

recommendations.title: Embed assistant output or add richer continuation scoring
recommendations.detail: Assistant output now contributes word-overlap scoring, but Examples.load still embeds only exampleIntentText. Add a second embedding for assistantOutputText and use it when the latest user message looks like a continuation rather than a new intent. Cheap to add; helps multi-turn conversations where the user references a previous action.

recommendations.title: Extend example caching beyond promptConvo retries
recommendations.detail: Prompter.promptConvo caches $EXAMPLES inside one retry burst via stableReplacements (prompter.js:284-356). The next cache boundary is the handleMessage/self-prompt loop: reuse the selected example set while the normalized latest intent is unchanged, and invalidate only when a new user/system intent arrives.

themes.title: Long-Horizon Planning & Skill Libraries
themes.summary: ObjectiveStack, mining-objective helpers (now with recordMiningCompletion writing to MemoryBank), and SkillLibrary exist, but the bot still does not grow new reusable skills at runtime. Voyager's central thesis is that the skill library should be a write-back store that compounds over a play session.

recommendations.title: Make SkillLibrary writable: persist successful !newAction code as named skills
recommendations.detail: When a !newAction execution succeeds AND produces a useful inventory delta, prompt code_model to (a) name the function, (b) write a one-line description, then save to bots/{name}/skills/{name}.js and re-embed it into skill_docs_embeddings (skill_library.js:9-66). Next time getRelevantSkillDocs runs, the model sees its own successful prior code as a callable. Literally the Voyager loop and the highest-impact long-horizon change available.

recommendations.title: Add a curriculum proposer that generates the next sub-goal
recommendations.detail: Add Prompter.promptCurriculum invoked when ObjectiveStack is empty and SelfPrompter is active. It takes current inventory + memory + recent skills + session_memory.pendingTasks and returns one 'next sensible sub-goal' (e.g. 'craft a stone pickaxe'). Voyager's automatic curriculum — replaces the current pattern of relying on the user to set top-level goals.

recommendations.title: Decompose top-level goals via GITM-style hierarchical decomposer
recommendations.detail: Wrap user-issued goals (the things fed to SelfPrompter.start) through a one-shot decomposer that returns a tree of sub-goals pushed onto ObjectiveStack. GITM showed this lifts ObtainDiamond success from ~30% to 67.5% versus flat planning, on essentially the same models.

recommendations.title: Add skill versioning and self-test before promotion
recommendations.detail: Before persisting a new skill from !newAction, run it again in a verification harness (no-op dry run, asserts no exceptions) and only commit on success. Voyager's iterative-prompting + self-verification step is what keeps the library from being polluted by code that worked once by luck. Without this, the library becomes net-negative within a few sessions.

recommendations.title: Annotate skills with preconditions and use them as retrieval boosts
recommendations.detail: When saving a skill, also record preconditions (required inventory, required nearby blocks) extracted from the prompt. SkillLibrary.getRelevantSkillDocs can then filter+boost skills whose preconditions match the current $STATS/$INVENTORY. Turns retrieval from 'most semantically similar' into 'most actually executable right now'.

themes.title: Eval & Observability
themes.summary: TranscriptLogger captures rich telemetry (chat / model / command / memory / lifecycle / objective events with stable codes), and there is now a docs/code-review/ directory for periodic audits. Still no replay tool, golden trajectory suite, or LLM-as-judge harness — without these, every prompt/runtime change is hard to validate.

recommendations.title: Build a transcript-replay harness that re-runs prompter on saved trajectories
recommendations.detail: TranscriptLogger records model.request/response pairs (transcript_logger.js:27-58). Add a script that takes a saved transcript and re-runs Prompter.promptConvo with the same history slice but the current code/profile, then diffs the response. Lets you safely iterate on prompts without spinning up Minecraft, and is the foundation for everything else in this theme.

recommendations.title: Curate ~30 golden trajectories (5 per task type) and run them in CI
recommendations.detail: Pick representative successful runs from bots/*/histories and freeze them as golden_trajectories/*.json with the expected sequence of command names. CI replays each, asserts the new model still issues commands of the same name in the same order (loose match, not exact args). Catches the 'I changed the prompt and now the bot won't mine' regressions.

recommendations.title: Add an LLM-as-judge scorer for full trajectories
recommendations.detail: For non-deterministic eval, write a judge prompt that takes (goal, trajectory, final_state, session_memory snapshots) and returns {success, efficiency, errors_made}. Use a stronger model than the bot uses (e.g. Claude Opus when the bot is on a smaller Sonnet/Haiku). Run nightly across recent transcripts; dashboard the scores.

recommendations.title: Emit structured progress metrics per objective frame
recommendations.detail: ObjectiveStack records push/update/pop events to transcript (objective_stack.js:23-62). Also compute duration_ms, commands_issued, retries, inventory_delta, and final result code per frame and log them as objective.metrics. Gives a per-task efficiency view that's far more actionable than 'did the bot eventually finish'.

recommendations.title: Add a 'shadow model' mode that runs a second model in parallel and diffs
recommendations.detail: When settings.shadow_model is set, fire promptConvo at both chat_model and the shadow in parallel, log both to TranscriptLogger, but only act on the primary. Cheap; gives continuous A/B data on cheaper-model viability with zero user-visible behavior change.

themes.title: Multi-Model Routing & Cost / Latency
themes.summary: Prompter supports separate chat/code/vision/embedding models from profile, and has a new-action planning call, but routes most text calls statically through chat_model. _model_map.js auto-discovers adapters by static prefix (models/_model_map.js:10-76), so adding a 'cheap_model' is mostly a profile-schema and routing change.

recommendations.title: Route 'easy' calls (memory summary, bot-responder, intent classify) to a cheap model
recommendations.detail: promptMemSaving, promptShouldRespondToBot, and promptNewActionPlan all use this.chat_model (prompter.js:400-479). Add profile.cheap_model and route non-action or pre-action planning calls there when stakes are low. Reserve the strong model for main reasoning, high-stakes command selection, and code verification.

recommendations.title: Implement a draft-then-verify cascade for !newAction code generation
recommendations.detail: promptCoding goes straight to code_model. Generate with a fast model (Haiku/Qwen-coder), then send the code to a stronger verifier with 'Will this run? List bugs.' Only re-generate with the strong model if verifier flags issues. Speculative cascades from Google Research show this beats either pure approach on cost-quality.

recommendations.title: Add a confidence-based escalator for command selection
recommendations.detail: When the model emits a command, classify the command/result context as high-stakes (mining, combat, irreversible building, route digging) or low-stakes (chat/query). If high-stakes and the generation came from a cheap model, re-prompt with the strong model before executing. This pairs naturally with ObjectiveStack status, session_memory.currentResourceTarget, and stable ERR_* command codes.

recommendations.title: Track per-model latency / failure rates and route adaptively
recommendations.detail: TranscriptLogger has model.request/response/failure events with duration_ms (prompter.js:295-326). Aggregate per-model rolling windows of (avg_latency, hallucination_rate, retry count) and demote a model temporarily when it crosses thresholds. Important since Mindcraft supports ~15 providers via _model_map.js with very different reliability profiles.

recommendations.title: Validate the embedding model at startup; don't silently fall back
recommendations.detail: Prompter.constructor falls back to {api: chat_model_profile.api} with no model name when profile.embedding is missing (prompter.js:80-93) — for several providers this either fails silently or returns degraded vectors. Either require an explicit embedding model in the profile (validate at startup) or pin a known-good default like text-embedding-3-small. Today, retrieval quality silently varies by provider.

bigger_bets.title: Full Voyager-style lifelong skill library with automatic curriculum
bigger_bets.rationale: Combine the writable SkillLibrary, the curriculum proposer, and the iterative-prompting + self-verification loop into one system that runs across sessions. The difference between a chat-driven assistant and an agent that gets measurably better the longer you let it play. Voyager reported 3.3× more unique items and 15.3× faster tech-tree milestones — achievable here because Mindcraft already has the scaffolding (Coder, SkillLibrary, ObjectiveStack, session_memory.pendingTasks).

bigger_bets.title: Multi-agent debate / specialist swarm for hard objectives
bigger_bets.rationale: Spawn ephemeral specialist personas (Planner, Critic, Coder, Navigator) for hard objectives, run a 1-2 round debate via convoManager (which already handles inter-bot conversation), and have the main agent execute the consensus plan. Mindcraft uniquely already has multi-bot infra in place — most agent frameworks would need to build that first. Pairs naturally with cascade routing: cheap model for specialists, strong model for the moderator.

bigger_bets.title: Memory-augmented multimodal planner using the existing vision pipeline
bigger_bets.rationale: VisionInterpreter and promptVision are wired up but underused — most reasoning happens off text-only $STATS. Adopt JARVIS-1's pattern: at planning time capture a screenshot, embed it alongside the textual state (which now includes session_memory + memory_bank summary), retrieve top-k similar past situations from the proposed episodic store, prompt the planner with both. Unlocks tasks where text descriptions are lossy (build aesthetics, complex terrain, base layout) and gives a clean place to put the multimodal memory store the codebase doesn't yet have.

bigger_bets.title: Typed/persisted POI layer auto-injected into $MEMORY
bigger_bets.rationale: Extend MemoryBank's typed namespaces into a first-class POI system: durable {kind, name, position, last_seen_at, last_verified_at, source} entries auto-injected into the prompt when the bot is within radius R of one. Today places/storage/observations all live separately; a unified POI layer with TTLs and confidence scoring would replace the ad-hoc 'last_death_position' / 'home_chest' / 'mined_*' patterns and feed cleanly into formatSessionMemory's surfaced labels.
